Base Labs server (qev, the model card's loader), self-hosted, BF16

27B dense, as the maker states it (counted from the released files: 27.36B). language model with its LM head + 0.46B vision encoder; source: counted from the checkpoint's safetensors, baselabs/mammoth-1@61cec44, huggingface.co/baselabs/mammoth-1; read 9 November 2026

Base Labs' released mammoth-1 weights (baselabs/mammoth-1 at 61cec44), a decision model post-trained from Qwen3.5-27B that also reads images. It ran on our hardware through its model card's loader (qev's DecisionEngine from OneJev at 81ce62f with the checkpoint's serve.patch, as the card's setup.sh installs it) behind our HTTP server (servers/baselabs_server.py), one request at a time. That runtime reads images only through an engine the patch leaves without the attention the model was trained with, so it is not on the Page images tab. The card mentions a trained "I don't know" option, but its answers have no such output, and our questions offer five options. Probabilities rounded to 6 decimals by the model's own loader. They sum to 1 only within that rounding, and the check before its runs allowed for it. Its card lists English only.

Latency: the time from sending one request to receiving its answer, measured from our computer, network and any retries within the request included. Request time: the time at least one request was in flight, over the requests whose answers were kept. It is not the run's elapsed time: it leaves out requests that failed and any pause before a run was resumed.
